newsitem.title: USA: BPA raises Friday firm peak power $1.50-2.00/MWh.
newsitem.headline: BPA raises Friday firm peak power $1.50-2.00/MWh.

text.p: The Bonneville Power Administration (BPA) raised its next-day offer prices for firm power during peak demand hours by $1.50 to $2.00 per megawatt hour (MWh), the agency said Thursday.
BPA also limited sales volumes for peak and off-peak firm sales on Friday to 200 megawatts.
Non-firm next-day offers were also limited to 200 MW, while no non-firm power was offered during peak-demand hours.

For Friday, BPA offered power during heavy load hours at $25.50 per MWh in the Northwest, up from $23.50 for Thursday sales. California-Oregon (COB) and Nevada-Oregon (NOB) border offers were $26.50, up from $25.00.

The federal power marketing agency also offered power during light load hours on Friday at $19.50 for both the Northwest and COB/NOB, while no surplus power was offered during those hours for Thursday pre-schedulings.
BPA also offered up to 200 megawatts of non-firm power during off-peak hours on Friday at $18.50 to $20.00, up from $18.00 to $19.00 per MWh for Thursday pre-schedulings.
